I've pulled the logs (see invite-accept-log-20261014.txt). Summary: when an invite is created we encode a token that includes the expiry date in ISO (YYYY-MM-DD). During accept we parse either the token or the client-sent expiry as a sanity check. In these failing sessions the client is POSTing acceptPayload.expiry = "14/10/2026" which our client-side validator attempts to parse as MM/DD/YYYY and rejects it as month=14 -> error. The server-side fallback does not accept the raw client string and returns 400 which manifests as the page reload/error Tanya attached.

Immediate remediation options (ordered by speed):
1) Ops manual invite with normalized ISO expiry (15–30m per batch) — lowest risk.
2) Server-side tolerant parse: accept DD/MM/YYYY and MM/DD/YYYY plus ISO (a short patch) — ~2–3 hrs + canary + DB migration to update tokens.
3) Client-side quickfix: detect locale and normalize before POST — ~1–2 hrs but requires front-end deploy across CDNs.

I recommend ops manual invites for tonight and a server-side tolerant parse tomorrow morning behind a feature flag. I'll prepare a small patch (PR) and tests. Ben, can you authorize the manual invite run and communicate timeline to the customer?

Karthik Iyer
